This is what happens when you've got a long coherence length, and don't pay attention to what's visible to the plate. This is a transmission hologram, 654 nm, but replayed with 532nm light.

[/img]

posts.topic_title: Transmission hologram and long coherence length
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Transmission hologram and long coherence length
posts.content_md: This is a very good point! Take your holograms and look around them for any uncarded optics. The hologram will tell! Any extra information stored on the plate will decrease your brightness. Depending on the spatial frequency perhaps by half!

posts.topic_title: Transmission hologram and long coherence length
posts.author: tpark
posts.post_subject: Transmission hologram and long coherence length
posts.content_md: Good points, all. I've got some holograms where I've knocked something over in the object, and for some reason I found it highly amusing - it was hard to keep still doing the exposure. But again, I'm a hack, so I probably get more bad holograms than those who are careful about everything.
